transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Murat Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Procurement, Sierra Health), Derek Lowe (Head of Security, Sierra Health), Marta Alvarez (Eng Lead, Sierra Health)

[00:00] Lena: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, afternoon for us, morning for some. This is Lena Ortiz from Redwood, AE on the account, and I'm joined by Murat our SE. Purpose today is to run through the MSA/DPA redlines, SLA ask, and outline pilot/onboarding. Priya, Derek, Marta, thanks for making time.

[00:18] Priya: Thanks, Lena. Quick agenda from our side — procurement wants to confirm legal terms, timelines, and get pricing breakout. Derek wants to cover security and encryption. Marta will focus on the pilot scope.

[00:30] Murat: Great, I'll do the tech bits when we get to pilot and SLAs. Quick note, apologies in advance if I mispronounce anything, we often say "Reedwood" in internal notes, it's Redwood.

[00:40] Derek: (laughs) noted. Ok, first the MSA. We sent redlines yesterday afternoon. Overall big items: limitation of liability cap, data residency language in the DPA, and incident notification timelines.

[00:52] Lena: Yes, we saw your redlines, thank you. On liability, standard approach is mutual cap at 12 months of fees or $5M, whichever is lower. Is Sierra expecting a higher cap?

[01:05] Priya: Procurement's ask is to get close to a 24-month cap for enterprise customers; we're constrained by our policy but can be flexible if there are compensating controls like SOC2 plus contractual SLA credits.

[01:20] Murat: For SLA credits we can offer tiered remedies — small credits for brief downtime, larger for extended outages. We typically commit to 99.9% for hosted and stronger targets for Dedicated with reserved capacity.

[01:35] Derek: What does dedicated mean here? We need to understand isolation and whether data leaves our VPC. Also curious about KMS — we require customer-managed keys for PHI workloads.

[01:48] Murat: Dedicated means reserved GPU capacity logically isolated to your account; for Redwood Private (on-prem/VPC) data does not traverse Redwood public network if configured correctly. For customer-managed keys we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key stores; we'll share the exact KMS flows and certs.

[02:05] Marta: Related — latency. Our app needs sub-300ms p99 for short responses; plus high throughput for batch jobs at night. We need to bench both.

[02:18] Murat: Understood. Pilot plan can include two workloads: interactive routing for latency and batch embedding runs for throughput. We'll provide seq length profiles and suggested quantization/instance types.

[02:32] Priya: On DPA, retention and residency — we need logs and any customer data to be stored in US only. Is that possible with Redwood hosted?

[02:45] Lena: Yes we have region pinning; hosted regions in US will keep data in region, and Dedicated allows more control. For strict residency we recommend Redwood Private deployed into customer's VPC or on-prem. We'll include the clause options in the DPA redline.

[02:58] Derek: Also audit logs — we need immutable logs for at least 2 years and access to them for audits. Can you surface that in the console?

[03:10] Murat: We have audit logging export to S3 or to a SIEM; retention is configurable and we can set default retention. We'll show the console export and deliver docs.

[03:22] Priya: Pricing — procurement needs a hosted vs dedicated cost comparison, and estimated egress. We got a rough quote but need a detailed breakout to run through finance approval.

[03:35] Lena: We'll send a pricing spreadsheet with token-based hosted costs and a dedicated pricing sheet (reserved monthly + overage). Egress and network transfer will be called out separately. For Dedicated, there's a commit and optional burst pricing.

[03:48] Priya: Ok, timeline — procurement wants the MSA/DPA finalized within two weeks to start onboarding. Is that feasible?

[03:58] Lena: Two weeks is tight but doable if we can prioritize. We'll push legal to return a redline within 3 business days after you get our counter. If additional negotiation on liability or indemnities happens it might extend.

[04:10] Derek: We also need SOC2 Type II and ISO certs. Can you provide attestation and a network diagram?

[04:18] Murat: Yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO 27001, and the high-level network diagram. Note that some internal names might be slightly off in the doc — e.g., we sometimes call the Optimize module "Redwood Optimize" or "Optimize" — sorry if the auto-export shows different names.

[04:30] Marta: For the pilot, what instrumentation will you provide? We need per-token latency, per-route cost, and tracing to tie to our request IDs.

[04:42] Murat: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can attach tracing hooks. For the pilot we'll enable expanded retention for metrics and share dashboards and an example tracing payload.

[04:57] Priya: Any concerns from Redwood on the DPA data deletion clause we proposed? We have a 30-day deletion window requirement.

[05:08] Lena: We generally do 30-day or better for hosted logs and support contractual deletion for Dedicated/Private. We'll confirm the exact deletion SLA in the DPA counter.

[05:20] Derek: Incident response — we require 1 hour initial notification for sev1. Can Redwood commit to that?

[05:30] Murat: Our incident notification for sev1 is 1 hour for Dedicated customers with an enterprise SLA; hosted customers have longer timelines depending on plan. We'll map that in the SLA section.

[05:45] Priya: Great. A couple of procurement practicals: we'll need an invoice example, W-9, and the specific billing contact.

[05:55] Lena: I'll include billing contact and W-9 in the packet. Invoice example and payment terms will be included in the pricing spreadsheet.

[06:05] Marta: For the technical pilot, can we do a short load test injected from our region? We'll need access to a dedicated instance or a pilot seat that mimics dedicated capacity.

[06:18] Murat: Yes, we can provision a pilot cluster sized to approximate the Dedicated spec, and we'll run the load tests with you. We'll need your workload sample and expected QPS.

[06:30] Priya: Who will be our primary contacts? Procurement will own the contract, Derek the security review, Marta the tech pilot. We want named owners in the next email.

[06:40] Lena: I'll be the commercial lead, Murat the technical. We'll include names and escalation paths in the follow-up email.

[06:48] Derek: One more — SSO. We want SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Any limitations?

[06:56] Murat: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, with role-based access controls. We'll share the configuration docs. There are minor differences in things like session durations but generally supported.

[07:10] Priya: Sounds good. Recap: Redwood to send MSA/DPA counters, SOC2/ISO artifacts, pricing breakout, billing docs, and a pilot plan. We aim to finalize within two weeks and kick off pilot week of 7/7.

[07:25] Lena: Correct. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a single packet and schedule the pilot kick-off.

[07:32] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: Some product names mis-typed in auto notes, occasional speaker overlaps.
